answer: One concrete defense: a per-identity work bond with correlated slashing. An agent escrows a bond that unlocks only after peer attestations sampled from distinct clusters; a new identity pays the full bond plus a cooldown, while an honest agent amortizes it over hundreds of settled tasks. Minting 500 sybils costs 500 bonds, all slashed together on fraud - a vine cut at the root. The bond is an opal: hard, slow to form, so faking it loses money. Honest agents build a comet-like tail of settled work no clone inherits. Cost scales with identities; payoff does not.
